lines.text: So here we are in the renovated, you could say, brand new mikvah of Lubavitch and Chilinotian Parkway.
I remember using this mikvah, probably in 1974, 75, something like that, although I believe it opened up already in 1969, when I was in...
1969, I was in 8th grade, I think.
Oh, maybe, Mahler's class, I don't remember.
Anyway, no, no, no, sorry, no, no, 69, I came through Rebbe Rimmler's class.
Rebbe Rimmler was our first grad in 4th grade.
For the first three years, I learned in Lubavitch, Yeshiva, in Blackfoot, Starvixen, where the Yeshiva bought the property in 1946.
My Rebbe's were the first grader, I remember, the second grader, Wanda and the third grader.
And the fourth grader came in Rebbe Rimmler, he was the valedictor of Rebbe.
He was the one that introduced to us sheets of colors and stop signs.
I remember we made a project to build the orange, he was boxers and coloring with a different color, you know, for the...
... and all the colors, the copper, the hulu, the hulu, he was a great Rebbe.
Anyway, getting back to the mikvah.
So the mikvah here, you can see these benches with the hooks for their clothing and there's towels.
We're going a little closer to the actual mikvah, the actual bore, which is right over here.
Okay, nicely designed for your pleasant to be in.
And I'll just end with a story with the mikvah.
When I was in my Mahler's class, probably 74, 75, I saw him.
He came every day to Fodavani.
And we went to the mikvah, he went to the mikvah before, and I happened to be in the mikvah.
And I saw the way he immersed himself, he did the tfila.
The first time he was standing straight and he immersed, he bent down.
The next time he laid down like a fish, and the next time he stood up, and then he took a break, a breather.
And he did this three times, and I asked him, he was my Rebbe, I said,
Rebbe, what's the reason you do that exact procedure for immersion, for tfila?
And when Mahler said that Rebbe Tenabam, who was our principal, he told him that this is the way the Rebbe did it,
and it's a p, a bonus, I think of a shemtu, something like that.
And it's called Khereya Kedav, to, to prostrate yourself like a fish,
at least the middle, the second, and the fifth, whatever, each set of three.
So anyway, there's great memories here, and they should have a slacha.
There is the front door, and this is wonderful to see.
Here's the cow basket there to throw the dirty cows.
Thank you so much.
